title: Coherence for section-normalized recorded derived pullback
statement: The recorded derived pullbacks [lem-pc-recorded-pullback-composition] admit coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Composition is exactly the universal lift built from the original K-flat counits and the section-normalized tensor comparison [def-trf-two-term-determinant-data]. The left and right unit laws and associativity hold; the left unit law at the identity is the normalization needed by the determinant data.

source.place: Tag 0D5S; sheaves.tex Tag 0097 for ordinary pullback comparisons.

proof.text: The original tensor adjunction and the section-normalized one have identical units on sections. The uniqueness characterization identifies them. Unfold mates to identify leftAdjointUniq after right-adjoint transport with the conjugate of pushforwardComp.

Rewrite the section-normalized composition lift as the recorded composition lift. Apply the existing derived pullback coherence theorem to the original retained counits and recorded composition isomorphisms. Its unit and associativity laws give the record fields.

For the Tor-window search, DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives a cohomologically bounded complex, without finite locally free terms. Zero hits. The separate "Perfect", "Tor" query returned unrelated perfect groups, perfect closures and graph matchings.

Two hits in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Complex/Determinant.lean concern complex numbers, not complexes. The additional leftAdjointCompIso search found the mate/composition API used in the proved normalized-coherence argument. No determinant construction was found.

mathlib_searches.query: Determinant line of two term perfect complexes compatible with affine base change and descent
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: LinearMap.det, IsBaseChange.det_endHom, LinearEquiv.det_baseChange, LinearMap.det_baseChange and related scalar determinants. These are endomorphism determinants, not determinant lines of complexes or compatible gluing data. The queried theorem types do not provide the required construction.
